newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Q1 budget deficit adjusted downwards.
newsitem.headline: Israel Q1 budget deficit adjusted downwards.

text.p: Israel posted a first quarter government budget deficit of 1.2 billion shekels, a 200 million shekel improvement on preliminary figures released last week, Treasury officials said on Thursday.

Updated figures released by Accountant General Shai Talmon adjusted the domestic component of the deficit downwards from 700 to 500 million shekels. The foreign component of the deficit stood at 700 million shekels.
The Treasury had planned on posting a surplus on the domestic side of the budget in the first quarter, officials said.
"Our analysis is reasonable but the revenues are smaller than we planned," Talmon said.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor, Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are due to meet on Sunday for an end of quarter review of spending and revenues.

The Treasury is studying whether the first quarter figures necessitate further budget cuts. Most Treasury officials oppose further cuts given the current weakness of the Israeli economy, officials said.
